title: Redwood security review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC - EnterpriseBank
summary: Redwood AE/SE run through SSO (SAML) setup, SCIM provisioning details, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Customer focused on integration with existing Okta setup, group->role mappings, audit log retention and KMS-based encryption. Agreed next steps: exchange SAML metadata, share SCIM attribute mapping doc, deliver RBAC matrix, schedule SCIM demo with test tenant, and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts.
next_steps: Redwood to send SAML SP metadata and quickstart doc (Lena)
Customer to share Okta app config and SCIM test workspace details (Aisha)
Redwood SE to prepare RBAC mapping template and least-privilege recommendations (Ethan)
Schedule follow-up SCIM demo and test provisioning (week of 12/14)
Redwood to attach SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation docs and audit-log retention options (Monica)
action_items: Lena: email SP metadata + quickstart by 2026-12-09
Aisha: provide Okta app screenshots and test SCIM workspace by 2026-12-11
Ethan: draft RBAC role matrix and mapping to customer groups by 2026-12-13
Monica: pull SOC2/ISO PDFs and KMS integration notes by 2026-12-10
Tom/Maya: confirm data residency requirement (EU vs US) by 2026-12-12
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-08 15:00 PST | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Lena Martinez, Ethan Cole, Monica Ruiz (Redwood) -- Priya Singh, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan, Dave Park, Maya Lopez (EnterpriseBank)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick security review focused on SSO SAML, SCIM provisioning and the RBAC model. introduce yourself quickly?
[00:10] Priya: hi i'm priya, ciso at enterprise bank. looking to validate least-privilege patterns and ensure auditability for regulators.
[00:20] Tom: tom here, platform lead, i'll own the actual integration work.
[00:25] Ethan: ethan, security/infra se at redwood. i'll walk through the scim flow and role mapping.
[00:30] Aisha: aisha, iam engineer, mainly okta configs and scim provisioning questions.
[00:40] Monica: monica from redwood security, i'll cover our SOC2/ISO artifacts and encryption/KMS notes.
[00:50] Dave: dave from compliance, quick questions on retention and audit logs.
[01:00] Maya: maya, devops, i'll help on network and vpc side.

[02:15] Lena: ok quick agenda, 1) sso/saml pairing and metadata exchange, 2) scim provisioning and group sync, 3) rbac model and least privilege, 4) audit logs, data residency, kms/encryption, 5) next steps. any additions?
[02:30] Priya: that covers it. also want to confirm timeline — pilot in january ideally.

[04:05] Ethan: on SSO, we support both SP-initiated and idp-initiated SAML flows. common pattern we see is okta as idp with a dedicated enterprise app. we'll provide SP metadata including ACS and entityID.
[04:40] Aisha: for okta, we usually do idp-initiated to test first, then switch to sp-initiated. any special claims we need?
[04:55] Ethan: yes we recommend sending persistent NameID and include email, groups, and a custom attribute for tenant_id if you use multiple workspaces. sometimes groups come through as a long string; scim is cleaner for provisioning though.

[06:20] Lena: note — we support SAML signing and require x509 certs for the sp assertion if you enable signed assertions. we also support encryption of assertions if required.
[06:40] Priya: we will need signed assertions and want to restrict assertion lifetime to 2 minutes. we also need SSO logout support.
[06:55] Ethan: that's fine, we can configure the assertion validity. logout works with both. small note, a lot of customers call the product re-dwood privet in transcripts, but it's Redwood Private.

[09:10] Ethan: moving to SCIM, we offer SCIM v2 for user and group provisioning. typical flow: create app in Okta, enable SCIM, provide SCIM base URL + bearer token, map Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[09:40] Aisha: which attributes do you require? first, last, email? do you support custom attrs?
[09:50] Ethan: required are userName, displayName, emails. we support externalId and custom attributes. group membership handling: we recommend syncing Okta groups with a single prefix, e.g., RBW_ to avoid collisions.
[10:10] Tom: can we sync nested groups? our org uses nested groups heavily.
[10:20] Ethan: SCIM standard doesn't natively do nested groups well. we recommend flattening via Okta transforms or a sync job. we can also accept a custom attribute that lists effective groups.

[12:00] Aisha: how do we map groups to roles? need an example of least-privilege roles.
[12:10] Ethan: typical roles we expose: admin, devops, deployer, viewer, billing. map Okta group names to these roles. best practice: minimal number of admins, use deployer for CI service accounts.
[12:35] Monica: on least privilege, are we supporting fine-grained perms like per-route or per-model?
[12:45] Ethan: currently RBAC is at route/model level and some resource scopes; we don't have per-token micro-perms yet. you can create custom roles with combinations of allowed actions.

[14:20] Dave: audit logs — what is captured? how long do you retain?
[14:30] Monica: we capture sign-in events, API calls, admin changes, provisioning events and model route changes. retention is configurable — hosted defaults to 90 days, we have add-ons for longer retention up to 7 years for enterprise.
[14:55] Priya: regulators may ask for 1 year of logs for certain workflows. what's the export format?
[15:05] Monica: logs are available via console export CSV/NDJSON and we support streaming to customer's S3 via secure transfer or pushing to syslog/ SIEM.

[17:00] Maya: any network considerations for private deployment? we are likely to require VPC peering and internal endpoints.
[17:15] Lena: for Redwood Private, we support VPC mode with customer-managed subnets, private endpoints, and optional on-prem package. for hosted we offer VPC peering for Dedicated.
[17:40] Maya: ok good, we'll need egress control and a short list of ip ranges.

[19:30] Ethan: back to SCIM: provisioning tokens should be rotated and stored in a secrets manager like AWS Secrets Manager. we support scim token rotation and can integrate with your vault via automation. service accounts for automation are recommended.

[21:10] Aisha: how do you handle deprovisioning — immediate disable vs soft-delete?
[21:20] Ethan: SCIM supports both; we recommend immediate deprovisioning for access but soft-delete for audit retention. we can configure to disable account and keep records for X days.

[23:00] Tom: about RBAC audit and admin escalation — what's the approval flow?
[23:15] Lena: Redwood doesn't provide built-in approval workflows yet; customers typically plugin their own ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow) and use group-based role changes via SCIM. we can flag that as a feature request if needed.

[25:30] Monica: on encryption, at rest data is AES-256; for customer-managed keys we support KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for dedicated/private.
[25:55] Priya: we require CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for our production data in dedicated mode. is that supported?
[26:05] Monica: yes we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private. hosted customers can use our managed keys; for Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM.

[28:10] Dave: does the audit trail include KMS key usage logs?
[28:20] Monica: KMS logs are available from the cloud provider side; we correlate key usage in our logs but the definitive KMS audit is in the provider's key management service. we can help map events.

[30:00] Ethan: data residency — we have regions in us-west, us-east, eu-west, and ap-southeast. you can pin accounts to a region or use Private for on-prem.
[30:15] Priya: we need EU-only processing for certain datasets. can you guarantee logs and backups remain in eu-west?
[30:25] Monica: yes, for EU residency we host data in eu-west region for that tenant and restrict backups to the same region; for stronger guarantees we recommend Redwood Private in your cloud project or on-prem.

[32:45] Maya: any pen-test or vulnerability scanning schedule?
[32:55] Monica: we conduct quarterly vulnerability scans and annual pen-tests; we can share the summary reports and remediation timelines in the SOC2 artifacts.

[34:20] Aisha: SCIM attribute mappings — can you share a sample mapping file?
[34:30] Ethan: yes we'll share a mapping doc. sample: Okta group "RBW_Admins" -> role "admin"; "RBW_Deployers" -> "deployer". include externalId to link to tenant.

[36:10] Tom: how do we handle CI service accounts? we prefer to create service accounts that are not tied to humans and rotate tokens.
[36:20] Ethan: recommended pattern: create a scim-provisioned service account with minimal privileges, assign to deployer role, and rotate its token monthly. we can automate rotation via API.

[38:00] Priya: SOC2/ISO — can you provide the Type II report and any ISO 27001 cert?
[38:10] Monica: yes we will provide SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation. redwood has both; we'll send redacted copies and an NDA if required for full reports.

[40:20] Lena: recap of decisions: signed SAML assertions, SCIM v2 for provisioning, groups->roles mapping with prefixing, immediate deprovisioning for access, audit export to S3 option, CMEK for dedicated.

[42:00] Dave: retention options confirmed. who is owner for RBAC mapping?
[42:10] Tom: i'll own internal mapping but want ethan's template.

[43:00] Ethan: we'll also include a short test plan: 1) exchange metadata, 2) test idp-initiated login, 3) enable SCIM in test org, 4) create groups and verify role mapping, 5) test deprovision.

[44:20] Aisha: can you do a live SCIM demo on follow-up?
[44:30] Lena: yes, we'll schedule a demo week of 12/14.

[46:50] Monica: last note on logging — admin events will include user, ip, timestamp, action, object id. we can push to SIEM and provide syslog connectors.

[48:30] Priya: regulatory Q: do you support exportable chain of custody for changes?
[48:40] Monica: our audit trails provide change history, we can provide exports for compliance.

[50:10] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and scheduling.
[50:25] Priya: thanks, appreciated.
[50:30] Tom: thanks all.

End transcript.
